content: 1. The subdermal buprenorphine implant and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should either be avoided or alternative medications should be considered. 2. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of transdermal buprenorphine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both transdermal buprenorphine and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 3. Long-acting injectable buprenorphine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 4. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 5. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Coadministration of cabazitaxel with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 6. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, reduce the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 7. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of calcitriol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 9. Carbamazepine decreases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 10. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Both ceritinib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. 11. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 12. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Cimetidine increases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of cisapride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Both citalopram and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 16. Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases the plasma levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 17. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Both clozapine and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 19. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. The use of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 20. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 21. Both crizotinib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 22. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 23. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of dabrafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 24. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 26. Lopinavir decreases the plasma levels of darunavir by increasing its metabolism. Conversely, lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both dasatinib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 28. Both degarelix and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Both desflurane and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 30. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 31. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 32. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Both dolasetron and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 34. Both donepezil and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 35. Both doxepin and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 36. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of doxepin cream by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 38. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 39. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 41. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both efavirenz and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 42. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 43. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 44. Both eliglustat and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 45. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 46. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 47. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. 48. Both encorafenib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Encorafenib is associated with dose-dependent QTc interval prolongation. 49. Both entrectinib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of enzalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 51. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 52. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 53. Both eribulin and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 54. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 55. Erythromycin base increases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases the plasma levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 56. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases the plasma levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 57. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases the plasma levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases the plasma levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 59. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 60. Lopinavir may alter the plasma levels of ethinylestradiol, leading to significant changes in estrogen levels. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 61. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 62. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 63. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 64. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 65. Lopinavir decreases the plasma levels or effects of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both fexinidazole and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 66. Both fingolimod and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 67. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, such as Cushing-type symptoms. 68. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 69. Both gemifloxacin and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 70. Lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs.
